self_contained_context.background:
Part of Phase 5: Cross-Platform Compatibility. Manual testing catches platform-specific issues automated tests miss. Emoji rendering
platform-dependent. Validates Rich library cross-platform capabilities.
self_contained_context.technical_context:
Perform manual testing on Windows, macOS, Linux terminals.

Testing platforms (if available):

**Windows:**
- Windows Terminal (recommended): Verify emoji display
- PowerShell 7: Verify emoji display
- CMD.exe: Verify fallback symbols work

**macOS:**
- Terminal.app: Verify emoji display
- iTerm2: Verify emoji display

**Linux:**
- GNOME Terminal: Verify emoji display
- Konsole (KDE): Verify emoji display

Testing checklist per platform:
- [ ] CLI launches without errors
- [ ] Character creation prompts display correctly
- [ ] Validation errors display in red
- [ ] Combat visualization displays emoji OR fallbacks
- [ ] Colors display appropriately (or degrade gracefully)
- [ ] HP color gradient works
- [ ] Victory banner displays correctly
- [ ] Exit confirmation works
- [ ] CTRL-C exits gracefully

Document results:
- Create docs/testing/cross-platform-results.md
- List tested platforms with status (PASS/FAIL)
- Note any emoji display issues
- Screenshot examples if possible

Fallback testing:
- Force emoji_enabled=False in CLIConfig
- Run CLI and verify fallback symbols used
- Verify functionality preserved without emoji

If only one platform available:
- Document limitation in roadmap notes
- Test emoji fallback mode thoroughly
- Note need for future multi-platform validation
self_contained_context.active_e2e_test: E2E Tests 5.1-5.2 (Cross-Platform) - should PASS when complete
self_contained_context.inactive_e2e_tests: All E2E tests except the active one should remain disabled with @pytest.mark.skip or similar

execution_result.summary: Cross-platform manual testing completed successfully with noted limitations - emoji mode fully working, fallback mode partial (combat events work, character cards hardcoded)

linux_wsl2.notes: Full Unicode emoji support; fallback works for combat events but character cards have hardcoded emoji

emoji_enabled_true.notes: All emoji displayed correctly, colors and gradients working as expected

emoji_enabled_false.limitation: Character creation cards display hardcoded emoji (🧙 ❤️ ⚔️ ⚡) instead of fallback symbols
emoji_enabled_false.root_cause: CharacterCreator._display_character_card() line 165 has hardcoded emoji in f-string
emoji_enabled_false.impact: Low - combat rendering (critical path) works correctly with fallback
emoji_enabled_false.notes: Combat events use config.get_symbol() correctly; character cards need refactoring (out of scope)

acceptance_criteria_results.fallback_validated: PARTIAL - Combat fallback works, character cards hardcoded
acceptance_criteria_results.color_display_validated: PASS - HP gradients and color transitions working
acceptance_criteria_results.functionality_cross_platform: PASS - All combat logic working identically in both modes
acceptance_criteria_results.fallback_mode_tested: PASS - Explicit fallback testing with test_fallback.py script

limitations: Only 1 of 3 target platforms tested (Linux WSL2; macOS and Windows not available)
Character cards have hardcoded emoji (CharacterCreator needs refactoring)
True emoji fallback necessity not validated (tested terminal supports Unicode natively)
recommendations: Test on actual Windows terminal (non-WSL) to validate true fallback necessity
Refactor CharacterCreator to use config.get_symbol() (future improvement)
Add --no-emoji CLI flag for easier fallback testing (future improvement)
